title: Binary Search: Find 1 Person in 8 Billion in 33 Guesses 🔍 (Java) | DSA #3 #shorts
description:
Binary search finds an item in a sorted list by always checking the middle. If the target is bigger, throw away the left half; if it's smaller, throw away the right half. Every guess halves what's left, so even 8 billion sorted names need at most 33 guesses (2³³ is about 8.6 billion). That's O(log n) time, and it only works when the data is sorted.

lines: Imagine a sorted list of everyone on Earth. Eight billion names. You can find anyone in thirty three guesses.
Don't start at the top. Open the list right in the middle, and compare.
Is your name after the middle? Throw away the whole first half. Before it? Throw away the second half.
Every guess cuts the list in half. Eight billion, four billion, two billion. After thirty three halvings, one name is left.
In Java, it's a loop with two indexes, low and high, moving toward each other. That's O(log n), but only on sorted data.
Check the middle. Halve it. Repeat.
